Team / Elena,

I've reviewed the NeuroMed redlines attached. High-level counsel view and recommended positions below — I put more detail in the attached draft response (Redwood_counsel_response_draft_20261103.docx). Main items to note:

- Retention: NeuroMed's 90-day ask for operational logs is restrictive for incident investigation and caching layers. Recommend offering a compromise: 90 days for plain-text request logs, 365 days for aggregated, anonymized usage metrics; allow extensions for security investigations with prior notice and retention minimization.

- Transfers & SCCs: We can propose the standard EU-US SCCs for now; for clinical data flows we should offer a Transfer Addendum (or execute SCCs at signing). Counsel flagged that NeuroMed may request contractual guarantees beyond SCCs — propose routing that to legal for limited carve-outs (e.g., no onward transfers without notice).

- Subprocessors: NeuroMed wants a 30-day notice + right to object. We can offer 30-day notice and a 10-business-day review window to object on reasonable security/compliance grounds; objections that would require service disruption are unlikely — propose an escalation clause to discuss alternatives (e.g., contractual safeguards).

- Incident notification & audit rights: current NeuroMed language asks for on-site audits. We should offer virtual SOC2 reports + annual self-attestation; provide an audit facilitation option (third-party assessor) at NeuroMed's cost for high-risk subprocs.

Action items for Redwood ops/security (Soojin): please attach the current subprocessor inventory and confirm which subproc handle patient-identifiable workflows vs. platform-only. Also confirm retention default values for logs/backups and whether we can carve a short-term retention exception for security investigations.

Planned path: Jordan consolidates our comments into a single reply to NeuroMed, attach SOC2, inventory, and our counsel draft; propose e-sign route and target dates.

Marissa Cole
